spans.s: rutā = ruta, voice, speech: in LV 〔286.20—21〕 (prose) read, ekarutā-(Lefm. ˚tāṃ, misprint?)-sarva-ruta-ravaṇī (Lefm. ˚racanī, v.l. ˚ramaṇī; our reading proved by Tib. skad cig gis skad thams cad sgrog pa daṅ, by one speech proclaiming all speech), ep. of the Buddhaʼs voice or speech; this form, in prose, confirms rutā in Mvy 〔482—3〕, cited s.v. ravita, despite the fact that the same passage in Sūtrāl. 〔xii.9〕, comm. (〔p. 80, lines 19—20〕) has ruta.
Rutāvatī (m.c. ˚ti), n. of a ‘deity of the sea’: Śikṣ 〔346.3, 5〕 (vss, from Ratnolkādhāraṇī).
-rutāvin (to ruta, cf. 〔§ 22.51〕), in sarvabhūta-˚vinaḥ Mmk 〔546.8〕 (vs), having the voices or cries of all creatures; perh. m.c. for *ruta-vant.
